description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself. Closed out 2026-05-08; substrate-convergence work in analyses 026-030 + the Geocities showcase landed the "Tweedles don't ship" bug class. P7 evals deferred behind P8 (operator interface) so the eval harness has a usable surface to run against.

phases.title: Observer API
phases.notes: HistoricalRunHandle reads any captured snapshot directory — parses run.log, reads the per-agent SQLite databases, loads the telemetry JSON, exposes summary() / meetings() / utterances() / per_agent_telemetry() / artifacts(). The replay-side surface that everything else in P8 sits on. Shipped 2026-05-07 alongside P8.2.

phases.title: TUI Inspector
phases.notes: Textual-based read-only TUI: snapshot library, run summary, meeting detail with body preview + speaker filter + utterance modal, artifact browser (global + meeting-scoped, attribution via bus not mtime), cast view, theme cycling, app-wide vim navigation. First public release — wonderland-ai 0.0.1 on PyPI 2026-05-08.

phases.title: Streaming + Mock Turtle
phases.notes: Foundation for live-watch UX. Extend RunHandle with stream_events() async iterator; HistoricalRunHandle defaults to yield-now (no behavior change for inspector); MockTurtleHandle replays a snapshot's events with compressed timing + dwell cap so we iterate live-watch UI against a free testbed. After P8.3 the TUI can subscribe to "events as they arrive" without caring whether the source is replay, mock, or eventually a real bus.

phases.title: Live-watch screen
phases.notes: New LiveRunScreen that consumes the streaming API — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator, live cost ticker, drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay so zero API spend during UX iteration. The screen that turns Wonderland from "things happen and you read transcripts later" into "things happen and you watch them happen."

phases.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
phases.notes: NewRunScreen — directive textarea, workflow picker (TDD/canonical/smoke), project-root picker. LiveRunHandle wraps a real Runner+Caucus, emits via the same streaming API as MockTurtleHandle so the live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably. The leap from "replay testbed" to "actually launches a real run." First end-to-end test: directive → live watch → artifacts → done.

phases.title: New-project spinup (the rabbit hole)
phases.notes: Three entry paths converging on a single project-context capture: greenfield (skeleton picker + scaffold), existing-Wonderland (already covered by P8.5's project picker), adopt-existing (wonderland init + stack-detection routine that pre-fills the context form from manifest files). Persists .wonderland/project-context.md in a forward-compatible shape so future workflow-context injection has one input format to read. The on-ramp that turns "pip install" into "team's ready to start."

phases.title: First-use polish
phases.notes: Welcome/home screen (new run / browse snapshots / cast / configure), error states (missing API key, no project root, run failure), abort flow (clean shutdown of running threads), quiescence indicator (M5's long pauses need "still working, just thinking"), README + SHOWCASE updates with the TUI flow. The rough-edges sweep that closes the gap between "works for the developer" and "works for someone who just installed it."

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

phases.title: Meeting turns: phases + priority + rotations
phases.notes: Per analysis 033 (analyses/033-meeting-as-mtg-turn.md): lift phases + priority rotation + turns-as-budget from MtG into the meeting engine; skip the stack. Sequenced as a substrate phase that alternates with P8's interface track per the back-and-forth-stays-fresh rhythm. Engine work is bigger than P8's per-task shape and benefits from its own phase boundary. Engine + workflow schema + observer events are P1 (load-bearing); rotation counter + failure-mode detectors are P2 (instrumentation that lands once the structure exists).

phases.title: Two-Headed Giant: team windows
phases.notes: Per the live r35-tdd-serial-phased observation: strict-serial priority within a rotation imposes ~N× cast size wall-clock cost on constitutionally-paired agents (Tweedledee/Tweedledum, Alice/Hatter) who in legacy mode would have deliberated concurrently. Phase 9.5 generalizes phases by adding team_groupings: list[list[str]] per phase. A team window opens concurrently for all team members via asyncio.gather; structural cap preserved (rotation budget × team count = bounded deliberations); §VIII observability preserved (per-agent WindowOutcome unchanged). Maps onto MtG's Two-Headed Giant format — paired players take their team turn together. The natural design follow-up to P9; lands once analysis 034 quantifies the wall-clock penalty of the strict-serial baseline.

activePhase.title: Meeting turns: phases + priority + rotations
activePhase.goal: Lift phases + priority rotation + turns-as-budget from MtG into the meeting engine; skip the stack. Per analysis 033. The substrate gains an outside-the-agent measurement primitive for §VIII failure modes (Hatter sprawl, Cat withdrawal, Tweedle iteration) — pass-vs-not-asked becomes engine-visible rather than transcript-inferred. First implementation behind a workflow opt-in so we can A/B against the 032 banner ($4.7236, 1080 LOC, 10 test files) with controlled variables. Headline acceptance metric: Hatter's M4 call count drops vs 032 without his test quality dropping. Constitutions do NOT change — phases + priority are engine-side, never surfaced in agent context (mitigation against the 030 F1 anchoring lesson).
activePhase.sequencing: Data model first (T55) — Phase, PriorityWindow, RotationBudget dataclasses with no behavior yet, so the engine and tests have stable types to reference. Then RunEvent additions (T56) — PhaseStarted, PhaseEnded, PriorityWindowOpened, AgentActed, AgentPassed, RotationCompleted — landing before the engine emits them so all three RunHandle implementations (Historical, MockTurtle, Live) gain replay/no-op handling first. Then workflow YAML schema (T57) — phases: per meeting block, default to a single 'discussion' phase when absent so existing workflows keep working untouched. Then the engine work itself (T58) — re-scope the engagement policy from 'who speaks next' to 'act or pass per priority window'; phase advances when all cast members pass in succession OR rotation-budget exhausts OR workflow-declared exit condition fires. Then the first opt-in run (T59) — add phases: to tdd-serial.yaml, run pomodoro through it, compare per-agent + per-meeting cost vs the 032 banner. Failure-mode detectors (T60) come last because they piggyback on AgentPassed events that don't exist until T56-T58 land.

tasks.title: Phase + PriorityWindow + RotationBudget data model
tasks.details: Pure data primitives, no behavior. Add to src/wonderland/meeting/turns.py (new module): Phase dataclass (name: str, exit_condition: Callable | None, max_rotations: int), PriorityWindow dataclass (agent_id, phase, window_index, rotation_index), RotationBudget dataclass (max_rotations, current_rotation, passes_this_rotation: dict[AgentID, bool]). Plus an enum WindowAction { ACTED, PASSED }. Tests cover construction + invariants (RotationBudget.all_passed_this_rotation(), RotationBudget.advance_window(), Phase.is_exhausted()). No engine wiring yet. ~150 LOC + ~80 LOC tests.
tasks.resolution: Shipped src/wonderland/turns.py: PhaseDefinition (frozen dataclass, validates name + max_rotations >=1), WindowAction enum (ACTED/PASSED), WindowOutcome (frozen, rejects PASSED+utterance_id combo), PhaseState (mutable, append-only outcomes; computed properties: current_rotation, windows_opened, all_passed_in_succession, is_exhausted, is_complete, next_agent; per-agent counts for T60). 25 tests cover construction invariants, rotation arithmetic (cycle through cast, advance after full rotation), three completion paths (succession/exhaustion/exit-condition), exit-condition overrides remaining budget, sprawl-shape and withdrawal-shape per-agent counts. Clean: 1431 tests pass.

tasks.title: RunEvents: PhaseStarted, PhaseEnded, PriorityWindowOpened, AgentActed, AgentPassed, RotationCompleted
tasks.details: Extend the RunEvent union in src/wonderland/observer/events.py with the six new event types. Update HistoricalRunHandle to no-op them on replay (older snapshots won't have them). Update MockTurtleHandle to skip them in basic mode. Update LiveRunHandle to translate them through. The events have to land BEFORE the engine emits them so observers don't blow up on unknown events. Tests: each event constructs cleanly, replay-paths handle absence gracefully, JSONL serialization round-trips.
tasks.resolution: Shipped 6 new RunEvent dataclasses in src/wonderland/observer/events.py: PhaseStarted (meeting_thread_id, phase_name, max_rotations, cast: tuple, exit_condition_artifact?), PhaseEnded (reason: succession/exhausted/exit_condition/aborted, rotations_used, total_windows, passes_per_agent, acts_per_agent — the §VIII observability primitive T60 will read), PriorityWindowOpened (agent_id, rotation_index, window_index_in_phase), AgentActed (utterance_id cross-references UtteranceEmitted), AgentPassed (optional reason — pass is first-class), RotationCompleted (boundary event, minimal payload). Extended RunEvent union + observer/__init__.py exports. 9 new tests added (34 total in test_observer_events.py). Backward-compat by construction: older snapshots simply don't have these events, all 3 handles work unchanged. Full suite: 1440 pass.

tasks.title: Workflow YAML schema: phases: per meeting, single-phase default
tasks.details: Extend the workflow schema in src/wonderland/workflow.py: each meeting block can declare phases: [{name, exit_condition_artifact?, max_rotations?}]. When absent, the meeting gets a single default phase named 'discussion' with max_rotations matching the existing budget logic — backward-compatible by construction. Validation: phases must have unique names, exit_condition_artifact must reference a declared artifact in the workflow, max_rotations >= 1. Tests cover the new schema + the backward-compat path against existing workflow YAMLs.
tasks.resolution: Shipped PhaseSpec Pydantic model in src/wonderland/workflow.py: name (required), max_rotations (default 3, ge=1), exit_condition_artifact (optional string). Added Meeting.phases: list[PhaseSpec] = default empty list — opt-in semantics, existing workflows unchanged. Validator on Meeting catches duplicate phase names. PhaseSpec.to_phase_definition() bridges workflow-side schema → engine-side PhaseDefinition (turns.py). 6 new tests cover the schema (defaults, declarations, duplicate-rejection, max_rotations validation, PhaseSpec construction, round-trip to PhaseDefinition). All 4 bundled workflow YAMLs (canonical/smoke/tdd/tdd-serial) parse unchanged via the parameterized integrity tests. Full suite: 1446 pass.

tasks.title: Engine: re-scope engagement policy to act-or-pass per priority window
tasks.details: The big one. In src/wonderland/meeting.py — replace the current 'who speaks next' loop with a phase-driven priority rotation. For each phase: rotate priority through cast in declared order, on each window the agent acts (one utterance + tool calls) OR passes (explicit no-op), advance window. Phase ends when (a) all-pass-in-succession (every agent passed without an act between them), (b) max_rotations reached, or (c) workflow exit_condition_artifact ships. Engagement policy stays heuristic-then-LLM but the LLM prompt becomes 'given your priority window, do you have something load-bearing to say or do you pass?' rather than 'should you speak now?'. Emit T56 events at the right moments. Constitutions UNCHANGED. Tests: act-or-pass invariants, phase advance triggers, rotation budget exhaustion, all-pass-in-succession detection, observer event emission.
tasks.resolution: T58a/b/c complete. Phased meeting engine ships end-to-end behind workflow opt-in (meeting.phases declaration). Priority gate via Utterance.recipients filter at the bus level; orchestrator drives compose_context+deliberate directly bypassing autonomous engagement; SpeechAct.PASS as first-class action; per-window asyncio.wait_for timeout (300s default); both meeting_budget and rotation budget apply; PhaseEnded events carry passes_per_agent + acts_per_agent for §VIII observability primitives. smoke-phased.yaml available for live verification. Live run + analysis 034 banner is T59.

tasks.title: First opt-in run: phases: in tdd-serial.yaml, A/B vs 032 banner
tasks.details: Add phases: declarations to src/wonderland/closet/workflows/tdd-serial.yaml — M3 (negotiate / settle), M4 (clarify / red-tests / wait), M5 (implement / verify), M6 (present / review / defend / verdict). Pick max_rotations per phase based on what 032 telemetry showed needed (M5 ran 3 iterations averaging 56 calls each — match that with rotation_budget=3 not call counts). Run pomodoro through it. Compare against 032 banner: per-agent cost (Tweedles were 71.9%, Hatter 19.1%), per-meeting cost (M4: $1.73, M5: $1.47 across 3 iterations), output volume (1080 LOC, 10 test files). Headline metric: Hatter call count drops without test quality dropping. Document outcome as analysis 034 (banner if good, post-mortem if not).

tasks.title: Failure-mode detectors: never-passes (sprawl), always-passes-after-first (withdrawal)
tasks.details: Now that the engine emits AgentPassed events, write detectors that piggyback on the existing synthetic-consensus guard pattern. In src/wonderland/guards/ (or wherever the synthetic-consensus guard lives) — never_passes_detector flags an agent who never passes a priority window across N rotations (sprawl shape, Hatter §VIII). always_passes_after_first_detector flags an agent who acts once then passes every subsequent window for the rest of the meeting (withdrawal shape, Cat §VIII). Detectors emit ObserverWarnings rather than failing the run — they're measurement, not enforcement. Tests with synthetic event streams covering both detection shapes + happy-path.

tasks.title: Priority-gate primitive: SpeechAct.PASS + Utterance.recipients + bus filter
tasks.details: Smallest substrate addition for option A. Add SpeechAct.PASS to utterance.py (procedural, not substantive). Add Utterance.recipients: frozenset[str] | None = None — when set, bus delivers only to those subscriber names regardless of thread roster. Update InMemoryCaucus.publish to apply the recipients filter (additional check after roster). Tests cover: PASS speech act constructs, default recipients=None preserves existing fan-out, recipients={'hatter'} delivers only to hatter.
tasks.resolution: Shipped priority-gate primitive: SpeechAct.PASS (procedural, partition test count bumped 5→6), Utterance.recipients: frozenset[str] | None field. InMemoryCaucus.publish filters delivery by recipients before roster check (bypass-roster observers still see everything — measurement remains whole-bus). RedisCaucus._consume applies recipients subscriber-side because Redis Streams fan out unconditionally — same caller guarantee. Tests cover: PASS classification, recipients=None preserves fan-out, recipients={hatter} delivers only to hatter, observer (bypass_roster=True) sees targeted utterances, JSONL round-trip preserves recipients (snapshots/replay safe). Full suite: 1453 pass.

tasks.title: Phase orchestrator: act-or-pass loop with T56 events
tasks.details: New module src/wonderland/meeting.py with run_phased_meeting(meeting, runner, ...) async generator. For each PhaseSpec: build PhaseState, loop while not is_complete: pick next_agent, publish a window-open Dodo utterance with recipients={agent}, watch for the agent's response (single utterance), classify as ACT (any speech act except PASS) or PASS, append WindowOutcome, emit T56 events at the right moments. Tests use a FakeRunner that scripts agent responses.
tasks.resolution: Shipped src/wonderland/meeting.py: 6 workflow-level event dataclasses (PhaseStartEvent, PhaseEndEvent, PriorityWindowOpenEvent, AgentActEvent, AgentPassEvent, RotationCompleteEvent — translated to T56 RunEvents by LiveRunHandle in T58c), helpers (_build_window_open_utterance with recipients={agent_id}, _classify_response, _phase_end_reason, _check_exit_condition), main run_phased_meeting async generator. Drives the act-or-pass loop end-to-end: opens windows in cast-rotation order, builds Dodo→agent window-open utterance, calls compose_context+deliberate directly via asyncio.wait_for(timeout=300s default), classifies response (None or PASS speech act → AgentPassEvent; else → AgentActEvent), advances PhaseState, emits RotationCompleteEvent at boundaries, ends phases via the four reasons (succession/exhausted/exit_condition/aborted). Uses setattr(agent, '_orchestrator_owned', True/False) defensively — the runtime flag for T58c's Runner integration. Both meeting_budget and rotation budget apply (Decision 4). 13 tests cover the orchestration shape end-to-end against FakePhaseRunner with scripted FakePhaseAgent responses. Full suite: 1466 pass.

tasks.title: run_workflow integration + first end-to-end smoke
tasks.details: In workflow.py's run_workflow / _convene_one: gate on meeting.phases — if non-empty, call run_phased_meeting; otherwise the existing path. Add a phased variant of the smoke workflow (or new test workflow) so we can run the full pipeline end-to-end. Verify against the existing smoke test pattern.
tasks.resolution: Shipped end-to-end phased meeting integration: WonderlandAgent._orchestrator_owned flag (listen() records to memory but skips pending.put when set, preventing autonomous deliberation during phased meetings); _run_one_meeting dispatcher in workflow.py routes to run_phased_meeting when meeting.phases is non-empty, _convene_one otherwise (strictly opt-in, legacy path unchanged); LiveRunHandle gains 6 isinstance branches translating PhaseStartEvent/PhaseEndEvent/PriorityWindowOpenEvent/AgentActEvent/AgentPassEvent/RotationCompleteEvent → T56 RunEvents (PhaseStarted/PhaseEnded/PriorityWindowOpened/AgentActed/AgentPassed/RotationCompleted). New bundled workflow smoke-phased.yaml — single-meeting two-rotation phased workflow for live verification. Integration test confirms run_workflow correctly dispatches phased meetings and event ordering: MeetingStartEvent < PhaseStartEvent < PhaseEndEvent < MeetingEndEvent. Full suite: 1475 pass. Snapshot persistence (writing phase events to disk for HistoricalRunHandle replay) deferred as follow-up.
